facts.text: Agawam’s name comes from a Native American village on the west bank of the Connecticut River, meaning “unloading place” or “fish‑curing place.”.
In 1636 William Pynchon bought land from the Agawam tribe for 10 coats, 10 hoes, and 10 fathoms of wampum, laying the town’s early foundation.
The Agawam Historical Association preserves the town’s past and runs the Agawam Historical and Fire House Museum at 35 Elm Street.
Agawam’s library history began when Minerva Porter Davis donated a building in 1924, creating the town’s first public library.
The town hosts the former Six Flags New England amusement park, once called Riverside Park, one of the largest parks in the U.S.
In 1953 WWLP, an NBC affiliate, opened studios on Provin Mountain in Feeding Hills, making Agawam a regional broadcast hub.
